title: Doubt that lasts until the Hour arrives without warning.
subtitle: Some wait for proof that comes too late
then: Qatadah said Allah's command catches people unaware, {trap}when they are proud and comfortable{/trap} and think punishment will never come. Ikrimah and Mujahid said the barren Day is the Day of Resurrection, after which there is no night.
now: You keep a question about faith on the shelf: I will look into it when life calms down. Years pass in meetings, school runs and holidays. {idea}The verse warns that some doubts are only settled by the Hour itself.{/idea}
old: I will sort out my doubts properly when I have time.
new: Certainty that waits for the Hour comes too late; I should seek it now.
try: Write down one faith question you have parked, and book time this week to study it.

title: On that Day, all sovereignty is Allah's.
subtitle: He judges, and the believers reach the Gardens
then: Ibn Kathir links this to Owner of the Day of Recompense. The believers are those whose {idea}words and deeds were in harmony{/idea}, who acted on what they knew. Their bliss never ends or fades.
now: The landlord, the boss, the official stamping your form all seem to hold your life in their hands. {reward}On that Day, none of them will have any say.{/reward} Only belief that you lived out will matter.
old: The people with power over me decide my future.
new: All real sovereignty is Allah's; I live for His judgment.
try: Do one thing today that matches what you say you believe.

title: Pride that turned from truth meets humiliation.
subtitle: The end of arrogant denial
then: Ibn Kathir says these were people who {trap}resisted the Messengers and were too proud to follow them{/trap}. The humiliation is in recompense for arrogantly turning from the truth.
now: You get into a debate and realize halfway that you are wrong, but your ego will not let you admit it. {idea}The verse shows where that pride ends up if it becomes a lifetime habit.{/idea} Humility today is the cure.
old: Admitting I am wrong would be humiliating.
new: Humbling myself now is far lighter than being humbled later.
try: Admit one mistake today, plainly, to the person it affected.

title: They left everything for Allah; He provides the best.
subtitle: The emigrants, whether killed or simply died
then: Ibn Kathir describes those who left {idea}homelands, families and friends for Allah and His Messenger{/idea}. Fadalah bin Ubayd, at two funerals, said he would not mind from which grave he was raised, the fallen or the one who died, because of this verse.
now: You moved cities for a halal job, or left a circle of friends that pulled you down. It was lonely and you lost a lot. {reward}The verse says what you gave up for Allah is never a loss{/reward}; He is the best of providers.
old: What I sacrificed for my faith is just gone.
new: Whatever I leave for Allah, He replaces with better provision.
try: Recall one thing you gave up for Allah and thank Him for what replaced it.

title: An entrance that will please them.
subtitle: Allah knows their effort and forbears their faults
then: Ibn Kathir says the entrance is Paradise. Allah knows those who migrated and strove for Him, and as the Forbearing {reward}forgives and overlooks their sins{/reward}, accepting their migration and trust as expiation.
now: You arrive at a new home after a long trip: someone has the lights on and the food warm. Imagine that, without end. {reward}The verse promises an arrival you will be pleased with{/reward}, from One who knows your effort and forgives your slips.
old: My flaws will cancel out the good I tried to do.
new: Allah sees my effort and is forbearing with my faults.
try: Tell Allah tonight about one effort no one noticed, and ask Him to accept it.

title: Wronged again after responding fairly, Allah will help.
subtitle: Equal response, and the door of pardon
then: Muqatil and Ibn Jurayj said it was revealed about a skirmish where {trap}the idolators insisted on fighting in the Sacred Months{/trap} though the Muslims urged them not to. The Muslims responded and Allah gave them victory. The verse ends: Allah is Pardoning, Forgiving.
now: A relative insults you at a gathering. You answer once, fairly, and they come back harder. Your thumbs hover over a long, cutting reply. {idea}The verse puts a limit on response, then points at Allah's pardon{/idea} and promises His help.
old: If someone hurts me, I can hit back as hard as I like.
new: A fair response has a limit; Allah's help and pardon are bigger than revenge.
try: Delete one reply today that goes further than what was done to you.

title: Night into day, day into night: He hears and sees.
subtitle: The One who shifts the hours can shift your situation
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}directs the affairs of creation as He wills{/idea}. Merging means one encroaches on the other: long nights in winter, long days in summer. He hears what His servants say and sees them.
now: You wake at 4am, anxious, in a dark kitchen. Then light slowly comes through the window. {reward}The One who does that every morning is the One who heard your worry in the dark.{/reward}
old: My hard season will never change.
new: The One who turns night into day can turn my situation, and He hears me.
try: Watch the sky change at sunrise or sunset today and make one dua then.

title: He is the Truth; everything else they call on is false.
subtitle: The Most High, the Grand
then: Ibn Kathir explains: He is the true God, {idea}whatever He wills happens{/idea}, and everything is in need of Him. Everything worshipped instead of Him is false because it can neither benefit nor harm. None is higher or greater.
now: Late at night you refresh your bank app, your inbox, your ex's profile, as if one of them will rescue you. {idea}The verse calls all of these what they are: not the Truth.{/idea} Turn to the Most High.
old: I need many things to hold my life together.
new: Only Allah is real help; the rest cannot benefit or harm on their own.
try: Before checking your phone first thing tomorrow, say a short prayer to Allah.

title: Rain falls, the earth turns green: He is Subtle.
subtitle: The kindness that reaches every hidden seed

row.title: subtle care
sub: each tiny seed gets its share

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}knows what seeds are in every region of the earth, however small{/idea}, and each gets its share of water. He cites Luqman: even a mustard seed inside a rock, Allah brings it forth.
now: You notice moss on a wall after a week of rain, or a weed pushing through a crack in the pavement. {reward}No one planted it. He knew it was there.{/reward} He knows the hidden seeds in you too.
old: My small, hidden struggles go unnoticed.
new: The Subtle One reaches every hidden seed, including what is buried in me.
try: Look for one small green thing outside today and say: Allah is Subtle.

title: Everything belongs to Him, and He needs none of it.
subtitle: The Free of need, the Praiseworthy

row.title: I need it
sub: He is rich, I am in need

then: Ibn Kathir says He owns all things and {idea}has no need of anything besides Himself{/idea}; everything is in need of Him and submits to Him. This follows the green earth: the rain and the growth are all His.
now: You hold your paycheck, your car keys, your child's hand. All of it feels like yours. {idea}The verse reminds you it all belongs to Him{/idea}, and He gave it while needing nothing back.
old: My prayers and good deeds are a favor I do for God.
new: Allah owns everything and needs nothing; my worship is for my own good.
try: Give away one small thing today, remembering it was His first.

title: Ships on the sea, and a sky held back from falling.
subtitle: Everything around you, made to serve you
then: Ibn Kathir describes ships moving gently through raging seas, carrying goods and people, and the sky withheld from falling {reward}by His kindness, mercy and power{/reward}, even though people do wrong.
now: Your parcel arrives from across the world. It crossed oceans on a container ship you never saw. Overhead the sky stays where it is, every single day. {idea}The verse asks you to see the kindness in what feels automatic.{/idea}
old: The world just runs; nothing special about it.
new: Every ship that floats and every sky that holds is mercy toward me.
try: When your next delivery or meal arrives, thank Allah for everything that carried it.

title: He gave you life, will take it, and give it again.
subtitle: And still people are ungrateful
then: Ibn Kathir asks: {idea}how can you set up rivals to Allah{/idea} when He alone created, provides and controls? He gave you life after you were nothing, will cause you to die, and will raise you. Yet people deny.
now: Birthday candles, a hospital wristband, a funeral program. Three paper things that mark your whole story. {reward}Every page of it is written by Him.{/reward} The verse ends gently sad: and still, people are ungrateful.
old: My life is mine to run however I want.
new: My life came from Him, returns to Him, and calls for thanks.
try: Thank Allah today for being alive, out loud, in one sentence.
